agree.reason: A skeptical committee member gets specific evidence (solo 3 a.m. shift, two missed shifts in three years, nine early mastitis cases worth about $8,000), and the two weak points are dealt with openly, so the letter is persuasive, though it never gives the applicant's full name and could get lost among 150 files.

honest.reason: Most claims match the brief, but three go beyond it: "no one else is on the farm at that hour", "the person who gets the most out of our herd management software", and the description of what the program trains people to do are not supported by the facts given.

works_the_facts.reason: The $8,000 saving and the nine cases are used well, but the attendance record stays as "two missed shifts" when it could be shown as roughly 2 out of about 780 scheduled shifts (5 a week for 3 years), which is clearer and more favourable.

right_comparison.reason: The letter never sets Tomás against a typical applicant or a typical farmhand, so the reader has no baseline for his attendance or his early detection of sick cows.

qualification.reason: The warning that written coursework will take him more effort is honest and backed by the failed-then-passed safety test and the night class, but it gives the reader nothing to check, such as a class end date or a level he has reached.

objections.reason: The five-week absence and the weak written English are both raised and answered with facts (his cousin covered his shifts, he came back on the promised day, he is taking a night class), and the letter does not invent any objection the brief already settles.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager with a signature and a phone number, but it uses only "Tomás" and never his full name, Tomás Reyes, and it has no date, both of which a committee sorting 150 applicants needs.
